subproblem.title: Extension of currents from U to ℝ^P by a smooth cutoff equal to 1 near a compact K ⊆ U
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open and K ⊆ U compact. Then there is a map E : 𝒟_{m+1}(U) → 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn U (m+1) → GeometricCurrentOn univ (m+1)) such that: (i) for every X ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(U) and every ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ K, (E X)(ω) = X(ω), where ω is regarded as a test form on ℝ^P (testFormOnInclusion); (ii) if X_j ⇀ X in U then E X_j ⇀ E X in ℝ^P; (iii) M(E X) ≤ M(X) for every X (total masses: massOn ℝ^P and massOn U, Simon 6.2.4–6.2.5); (iv) if X(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(U) whose topological support is disjoint from K, then spt(E X) ⊆ K and M(∂(E X)) ≤ M(∂X); (v) if some IMRep R in U represents X and R.carrier ⊆ K, then E X is integer multiplicity in ℝ^P. (In the proof E X(ω) = X(ζω) for one fixed smooth cutoff ζ.)
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (U K : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∃ E : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1) → GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1), (∀ (X : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)) (ω : TestFormOn U (m + 1)), tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (m + 1)) ⊆ K → E X (testFormOnInclusion (subset_univ U) (m + 1) ω) = X ω) ∧ (∀ (Xs : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)) (X : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)), WeaklyConvergesOn Xs X → WeaklyConvergesOn (fun j => E (Xs j)) (E X)) ∧ (∀ X : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1), (E X).mass ≤ X.mass) ∧ (∀ X : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1), (∀ ω : TestFormOn U (m + 1), Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (m + 1))) K → X ω = 0) → (E X).support ⊆ K ∧ (E X).boundary.mass ≤ X.boundary.mass) ∧ (∀ (X : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)) (R : IMRep U (m + 1)), R.Represents X → R.carrier ⊆ K → IsIntegerMultiplicity (E X))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the parent-supplied proof of cbr_closure_succ, step 8 (extension to ℝ^P: T̂(ω) := T(ζω) with a cutoff ζ ∈ C^∞_c(U) equal to 1 near K) together with the facts used in steps 9–11 (IM transfer, support, mass and boundary-mass bounds, weak convergence, agreement with the original current on forms supported in K). The vanishing hypothesis in (iv) replaces the appeal to (VO) in step 8: it is exactly what (VO) yields from spt X ⊆ K, and the localization child supplies it directly.

1. (Cutoff.) ℝ^P is locally compact and regular, so (Mathlib exists_open_between_and_isCompact_closure) there is an open V₁ with K ⊆ V₁, closure V₁ compact and closure V₁ ⊆ U, and then an open V₂ with closure V₁ ⊆ V₂, closure V₂ compact and closure V₂ ⊆ U. By the smooth Urysohn lemma in finite-dimensional real normed spaces (Mathlib exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff with smoothness order ∞, s := V₂ open, t := closure V₁ closed, t ⊆ s) there is a C^∞ function ζ : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with support ζ = V₂ and ζ(x) = 1 for all x ∈ closure V₁. Hence K₂ := tsupport ζ = closure V₂ is compact with K₂ ⊆ U, and ζ = 1 on the open set N := V₁ ⊇ K.
2. (Multiplication by ζ.) For a k-form ω on ℝ^P let ζω be x ↦ ζ(x)ω(x). If ω is a test form (C^∞, compact support), then ζω is C^∞ (product of C^∞ maps), support(ζω) ⊆ support ω so ζω has compact support, and tsupport(ζω) ⊆ tsupport ζ ∩ tsupport ω ⊆ K₂ ⊆ U. Thus ω ↦ ζω is a linear map M_k : 𝒟^k(ℝ^P) → 𝒟^k(U) (pointwise it is additive and commutes with scalars).
3. (Norm homogeneity.) For c ∈ ℝ and a k-covector α, the Euclidean coefficient norm satisfies |cα| = |c|·|α|: every coefficient α(e_I), I strictly increasing, is multiplied by c, so the sum of squares is multiplied by c² and its square root by |c|. Hence |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x implies |(ζω)(x)| = ζ(x)|ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x.
4. (Continuity of M_k.) Let ω_j → 0 in 𝒟^k(ℝ^P) (TestFormOnConverges): there is a compact K' with tsupport ω_j ⊆ K' for all j and, for every l ∈ ℕ, D^l ω_j → 0 uniformly on K'. Then tsupport(ζω_j) ⊆ K₂ for all j, tsupport 0 = ∅ ⊆ K₂, and K₂ is a compact subset of U. Fix i ∈ ℕ. For x ∉ K' we have x ∉ tsupport ω_j, so D^l ω_j(x) = 0 for every l (the support of the l-th derivative lies in tsupport ω_j, Mathlib support_iteratedFDeriv_subset); hence ε_{j,l} := sup_{x ∈ ℝ^P} ‖D^l ω_j(x)‖ = sup_{x ∈ K'} ‖D^l ω_j(x)‖ → 0 as j → ∞, for each l. Each D^l ζ is continuous with compact support, so B_l := sup_x ‖D^l ζ(x)‖ < ∞. By the Leibniz estimate (Mathlib norm_iteratedFDeriv_smul_le, in Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.ContDiff.Bounds), for every x, ‖D^i(ζω_j)(x)‖ ≤ Σ_{l=0}^{i} C(i,l)‖D^l ζ(x)‖‖D^{i−l}ω_j(x)‖ ≤ Σ_{l=0}^{i} C(i,l) B_l ε_{j,i−l}, and the right side tends to 0. Since D^i 0 = 0, D^i(ζω_j) → D^i 0 uniformly on K₂. So M_k(ω_j) → 0 in 𝒟^k(U), with the compact set K₂.
5. (Definition of E.) For X ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(U) put (E X)(ω) := X(ζω) = X(M_{m+1}ω), ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(ℝ^P). E X is linear, and if ω_j → 0 in 𝒟^{m+1}(ℝ^P) then M_{m+1}ω_j → 0 in 𝒟^{m+1}(U) (step 4), so (E X)(ω_j) → 0 by the continuity of X. Thus E X ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P).
6. (Proof of (i).) Let ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ K. For x ∈ K, ζ(x) = 1; for x ∉ K, x ∉ tsupport ω and ω(x) = 0. So ζω = ω pointwise; the inclusion into 𝒟^{m+1}(ℝ^P) does not change the underlying form, hence M_{m+1}(ιω) = ω in 𝒟^{m+1}(U) and (E X)(ιω) = X(ω).
7. (Proof of (ii).) If X_j ⇀ X in U then (E X_j)(ω) = X_j(ζω) → X(ζω) = (E X)(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(ℝ^P).
8. (Proof of (iii).) If ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(ℝ^P) is admissible for M(E X) (|ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x), then ζω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(U) is admissible for M_U(X) (steps 2–3), so ofReal((E X)(ω)) = ofReal(X(ζω)) ≤ M_U(X) = M(X). Taking the supremum over ω gives M(E X) ≤ M(X).
9. (Proof of (iv), support.) Assume X(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ∩ K = ∅. Let x ∉ K. As K is closed there is ε > 0 with ball(x, 2ε) ∩ K = ∅; let W := ball(x, ε). Then closure W ⊆ closedBall(x, ε) ⊆ ball(x, 2ε), so closure W is compact, contained in ℝ^P and disjoint from K. For ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ W, tsupport(ζω) ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ W is disjoint from K, so (E X)(ω) = X(ζω) = 0. Hence W lies in the zero region of E X and x ∉ spt(E X). Therefore spt(E X) ⊆ K.
10. (Proof of (iv), boundary mass.) Under the same assumption let η ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) with |η(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. By definition ∂(E X)(η) = (E X)(dη) = X(ζ dη). For y ∈ N the forms ζη and η coincide on the neighbourhood N of y, so their derivatives at y coincide, and since the exterior derivative at y depends only on the derivative at y (SimonGMT's exteriorDerivative is Mathlib's extDeriv, and Mathlib Filter.EventuallyEq.extDeriv_eq applies), d(ζη)(y) = dη(y) = ζ(y)dη(y). Hence δ := d(ζη) − ζdη, a test form in 𝒟^{m+1}(U) (ζη ∈ 𝒟^m(U) and d maps 𝒟^m(U) into 𝒟^{m+1}(U); ζdη = M_{m+1}(dη)), vanishes on N; so support δ ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ N, a closed set, whence tsupport δ ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ N is disjoint from K ⊆ N, and X(δ) = 0. Therefore ∂(E X)(η) = X(ζdη) = X(d(ζη)) = ∂X(ζη). As ζη ∈ 𝒟^m(U) is admissible for M_U(∂X) (step 3), ofReal(∂(E X)(η)) ≤ M_U(∂X) = M(∂X); taking the supremum, M(∂(E X)) ≤ M(∂X).
11. (Proof of (v).) Let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an IMRep in U representing X with M ⊆ K. Let R̂ have the same carrier, multiplicity and orientation, regarded in ℝ^P. All IMRep fields that do not mention the domain are unchanged (M Borel and countably (m+1)-rectifiable, θ measurable and ≥ 1 on M, ξ a.e. strongly measurable for H^{m+1}⌞M and orienting the approximate tangent spaces of M a.e.), M ⊆ ℝ^P trivially, and for every compact K' ⊆ ℝ^P, ∫_{M∩K'} θ dH^{m+1} ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dH^{m+1} < ∞, because M ∩ K' ⊆ M = M ∩ K and K is a compact subset of U (local integrability field of R). So R̂ is an IMRep in ℝ^P. For ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(ℝ^P), (E X)(ω) = X(ζω) = ∫_M θ(x)ξ(x)(ζ(x)ω(x)) dH^{m+1}(x) = ∫_M θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) dH^{m+1}(x) = R̂.action(ω), since ζ = 1 on M ⊆ K (the integrands agree on M). Hence R̂ represents E X and E X is integer multiplicity. ∎
proof_key_steps: Smooth cutoff ζ: ℝ^P → [0,1] with tsupport ζ compact ⊆ U and ζ = 1 on an open N ⊇ K (Mathlib exists_open_between_and_isCompact_closure, exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff).
ω ↦ ζω maps 𝒟^k(ℝ^P) linearly into 𝒟^k(U), keeps |ω| ≤ 1, and is sequentially continuous by the Leibniz estimate norm_iteratedFDeriv_smul_le.
E X := X(ζ·) is a current in ℝ^P; weak convergence passes through E.
ζω = ω when tsupport ω ⊆ K, so E X agrees with X there; M(E X) ≤ M(X).
If X vanishes off K: spt E X ⊆ K, and d(ζη) − ζdη vanishes on N, so ∂(E X)(η) = ∂X(ζη) and M(∂E X) ≤ M(∂X).
An IMRep in U with carrier in K, regarded in ℝ^P, represents E X because ζ = 1 on the carrier.

audit.reason: The prose and exact type agree on all five conclusions and hypotheses. The fixed cutoff and Leibniz estimate establish the required sequential continuity. The derivative defect vanishes near K, proving the boundary-mass bound under exactly the stated vanishing hypothesis. Transferring the compactly supported IMRep proves integer multiplicity. The proof is complete and independent of closure.
